Read: April 2023

As many people have said, much of what’s in it is stuff everyone already knows. Still, it works as an introductory book on investing.

I finished it about six months ago, and one idea has stayed vivid in my mind. The example goes roughly like this: buying a car is pure consumption, since a car starts losing value the moment it’s yours; buying a home is an investment, since you don’t pay rent and the home may go up in value.

Another example, roughly: a very ordinary man, the kind China’s officials once dismissed as “low-end population,” died, and people were astonished to discover he had investments worth several million. The takeaways: first, the power of compound interest; second, the habit of saving and investing.

I never had much desire for cars anyway, and after reading it I immediately decided my little car can keep going until it’s scrapped.
